rules.reasoning: The Tools page maintains strong design consistency with the Dashboard through shared components and centralized design tokens. The header structure is identical via shared Header component, navigation properly highlights the Tools link, and visual consistency is excellent with matching layout patterns, typography, colors, and responsive behavior. However, two issues prevent full compliance: (1) the search placeholder shows 'Search in tools catalog...' instead of the required 'Search tools...', resulting in partial credit, and (2) breadcrumb navigation is completely missing, which is a critical requirement. The implementation demonstrates good architectural decisions with shared components and design system, but lacks the specific breadcrumb feature required by the specification.

evidence.reasoning: Filter combination logic is partially implemented. The updateFilter function merges filter updates and resets pagination, and useTools hook passes all params to API. However, with department filter commented out and cost filter missing, only 2 filters (status + category) can be combined, not the full set of 4+ required filters.

evidence.reasoning: API integration supports multiple filter parameters simultaneously via query string, but incomplete filter implementation (only 2 of 4+ filters active) means full combination testing is not possible. Department commented out, cost missing entirely.

rules.reasoning: The Tools page implements a partial filtering system with significant gaps. Only 2 of 4 required filters are functional: category filter (fully working) and search field (integrated with global store). The status filter uses incorrect values (active/expiring/unused instead of Active/Inactive/Pending/All), department filter is completely commented out, and cost range filter is entirely missing. The reset filters button works correctly for available filters. However, there is no visual feedback system (badges, highlights, counts) to indicate active filters. Filter combinations can work for the 2 active filters (status + category + search) but cannot be fully tested due to missing filters. The implementation shows good architectural patterns (React Query, Zustand store, proper state management) but fails to meet the complete filtering requirements specified in the rule.

checkboxes.description: Success feedback shown after CRUD operations (toast, alert, message)

evidence.reasoning: Mutations only invalidate queries and close modal on success. No toast notification, alert component, or success message implementation found anywhere in codebase. Modal simply closes without explicit user feedback confirming operation succeeded.
onClose callback is the only success handler passed to mutations - no success message, toast notification library, or visual feedback mechanism present in implementation

rules.reasoning: Comprehensive evaluation of Tools page CRUD functionality reveals excellent implementation across 6 of 7 checkboxes. Add Tool modal opens with complete form containing all required fields (name, vendor, category, department, cost, status, URLs) with robust Zod validation. Edit functionality properly pre-fills form with existing tool data via defaultValues prop. Delete operation includes safety-first confirmation dialog with explicit warning and tool name display. Tools page displays significantly more data than Dashboard table (10+ fields vs 5 columns) including category, updated_at, description, and website_url. Pagination fully implemented with Previous/Next navigation, page indicators, and proper disabled states for 12 items per page. Form validation comprehensive with real-time onChange validation, error display, and constraints on all fields. However, success feedback is completely missing - no toast notifications, alerts, or success messages after CRUD operations complete. Modal simply closes without confirming to user that create/update/delete succeeded, which is a UX gap. Total score: 27/30 points (90%).

rules.reasoning: The Analytics page for Days 7-8 is completely unimplemented. The AnalyticsPage.tsx file contains only a placeholder div with the text 'AnalyticsPage' and no functional implementation. (4) No insights dashboard with the 4 required types: alerts, recommendations, cost optimization, and growth predictions. (5) No responsive or interactive chart features since no charts exist. (6) No date range picker or period selector. The page routing exists (src/routes/analytics.tsx) but leads to an empty component. This represents 0% completion of the Analytics page requirements worth 51 points total (50% of Days 7-8 conformity score). All 10 checkboxes marked UNCHECKED with 0 points awarded and confidence 1.0 due to clear absence of implementation.

rules.reasoning: The Analytics page exists but is minimally implemented with only a placeholder div. Navigation is fully functional with Analytics link properly integrated and highlighted when active (4/4 points). However, no charts are implemented - no charting library exists in package.json and the page contains only text (0/7 points for charts_color_palette). Typography cannot be evaluated as there are no typographic elements on the page (0/4 points). Layout grid follows the same pattern as Dashboard/Tools with px-10 my-10 flex flex-col gap-6, demonstrating consistency (5/5 points). The page is not responsive - it uses fixed px-10 my-10 instead of the responsive px-4 md:px-10 my-6 md:my-10 pattern used by other pages, and has no charts to stack responsively (0/9 points). Total: 14/34 points awarded. The Analytics page meets basic structural requirements but lacks the core content (charts, typography, responsive design) needed for full compliance.
